questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me that it was possible to take interesting courses in English and that the destination was located close to nature. I was also interested in the culture and way of living. I was looking for a smaller city, hoping for a more local and international experience with other exchange students, as I was the only Danish student during my semester.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. All information was available on the University of Lucerne website or through Mobility Online

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had one question about what to fill in on Mobility Online, and I simply sent an email to the University of Lucerne exchange department

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got offered accommodation at Student Mentor Foundation Lucerne (Eichhof) thought help form university Luzern

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The student accommodation, is the closest you get to on campus as Uni Luzern do not offer on campus accommodation. You live in studen apartments with other students from university and its only a 20 min walk from campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration was done through Mobility Online, and registration for help with finding accommodation was also available

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If help was needed, you could always email the Office of International Relations.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to take all the classes I wanted and could even sign up for more than required. This allowed me to try the classes before deciding which ones I wanted to continue throughout the semester. I also believe it is possible to attend classes without taking the exam, as you only need to decide which exams you want to take around mid-November.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you have to sign up for exams yourself.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think there were quite a lot of exams within a short period of time because I had to take many different classes (5 ECTS each), and the exam period for English courses is relatively short. The classes themself were interesting and educational

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I am used to a higher workload, with more required reading, at my home university, however the classes i have at home usually carry more ECTS points witch could explain this.

I think it was manageable to follow the courses even though they were master’s level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite similar, with seminar-style classes and a high level of interaction. Due to the small class sizes, there were no large lectures. I liked that some classes were broadcast, so I could rewatch them when sick or while preparing for exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Human Rights Law
International Banking & Capital Market Regulation
International Sports Law
Introduction to Swiss Law
Law and Society in a Global Context
International Law of Contemporary Media

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked the course Law of Contemporary Media, as it is very relevant since media plays an important role in globalization. You participate in a moot court as part of the course, which is an interesting way to engage more deeply with the topic.
I would also recommend Introduction to Swiss Law, as you gain a lot of background knowledge about the Swiss legal system, and the course includes some interesting excursions

I also would recommend Sports Law if you are into sports, is educational to learn about sport for a law perspective and is quite drifferent for the other classes i have taken.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Printing at the university is quite expensive, so it might be cheaper to buy legal texts from a bookshop.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food cost around 20% more, but it really depends if you eat out, cook with friends ect. 

Transportation was more expensive than expected, even tho you get the halbtax. 

Sports Classes was free through uni

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offers a wide range of different sports classes. They also invited us on a boat ride, dinners and a classical concert

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed going to yoga, and it was also a great way to meet new friends. I would definitely recommend going on hikes, as nature is very accessible from Lucerne.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend visiting Como, which is only a two-hour train ride away and gives you a real Italian vibe. I also really liked Lausanne and smaller cities during the summer.

 If you enjoy skiing, I would definitely recommend doing that, and even if you don’t, visiting mountain towns like Engelberg or Zermatt is still worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: We had a cultural class during the introduction week, where we became aware of cultural norms in Switzerland and potential misunderstandings. It is not very easy to become friends with local students, and most of your social life is with other exchange students. I also do not speak Swiss German. In everyday life, I did not experience many cultural differences.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be challenging if you do not speak German, but I did interact with local students through classes and yoga.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I had to adjust to a new culture, but I did not find it particularly challenging. Living with different cultures was more educational than challenging overall.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The love and respect for nature, as well as the international perspective in Switzerland.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is quite expensive, but you will learn a lot about cultures from all over the world and become very close to other exchange students, as you are not many studying abroad at the same time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I quite like being the only one form Denmark as you get to meet more for all around the world and make new internationalt connections. I also like it being a smaller uni, as you naturally get to know people you study with.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to travel around and experience Switzerland after a hard-working summer. It was also very rewarding once everything was settled with school and accommodation and you started making friends. It gave a feeling that the exchange would be a success.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was setting up a new everyday life with a new culture, new friends, and a new university. However, this was also where I learned the most.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
